stories.delivered_paragraph: Snap CEO Evan Spiegel declined to give investors preorder-demand figures for the company’s Specs smart glasses, saying potential buyers need hands-on experience ahead of a September launch event. The glasses cost $2,195 after more than a decade of development, far above Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses, which start around $350. The evasive answer leaves investors without an early gauge of whether Snap can turn its costly augmented-reality hardware bet into a consumer business.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Google is rolling out Google Health version 5.05 with direct syncing of Fitbit workouts, steps and vital-sign data to Apple Health. Previously, users could import Apple Health data into Google Health but needed third-party apps or workarounds to send Fitbit information in the other direction. The change makes it easier for people using Fitbit devices alongside iPhones to keep their health records in one place after Google replaced the Fitbit app in May.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon and B&H Photo have cut Samsung’s 32-inch M80F 4K smart monitor to $349.99, its lowest reported price and below its usual $400-or-higher level. The display doubles as a computer or console monitor and a Tizen-based streaming screen, with picture-in-picture, a removable webcam, USB-C charging up to 65 watts, and cloud-gaming apps. The deal targets buyers who want TV-style features without adding a separate television in a limited space.

stories.delivered_paragraph: AstraZeneca shares fell and Bristol Myers Squibb stock rose Monday after reports that the drugmakers were in deal talks, though neither company’s plans were detailed in the available reporting. A tie-up would combine two major cancer-drug businesses, but analysts described the prospective pairing as “odd” and questioned its strategic logic. Investors are now weighing whether the reported talks develop into a formal proposal and how a merger might reshape the companies’ oncology portfolios.

stories.delivered_paragraph: French commercial broadcaster TF1 has begun an early-stage process to sell its production-and-distribution arm, Studio TF1, hiring Rothschild to oversee it, Variety reported. The unit was rebranded only about a year and a half ago, while TF1 under president Rodolphe Belmer has been putting greater emphasis on streaming. A sale would signal a sharper focus on the broadcaster’s direct digital business while potentially separating it from its content-production operation.

stories.delivered_paragraph: House Democrats are privately considering whether to force a vote to expel Rep. Max Miller, an Ohio Republican, over domestic-abuse allegations he denies. Miller said Sunday that he would continue his reelection campaign and rejected claims involving his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and their young daughter; his former father-in-law, Sen. Bernie Moreno, called him a danger to his daughter. Expulsion is rare, but the prospect of one has reportedly prompted several congressional resignations this year.

stories.delivered_paragraph: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for coordinated action to strengthen EU borders after tens of thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain’s Ceuta exclave last week. Spain says about 69,500 people have returned to Morocco, while 72 people died on the Spanish side and 11 on the Moroccan side. EU interior ministers were due to hold emergency talks as the episode strains relations among member states and prompts renewed debate over Schengen travel rules.

stories.delivered_paragraph: “The Devil Wears Prada 2” drew 15.2 million global views in its first five days on Disney+ and Hulu, Disney’s biggest live-action streaming-film debut since 2024’s “Deadpool & Wolverine.” The sequel had already earned about $691 million worldwide in theaters, making its streaming start notable because it came more than two months after release. The result shows the fashion comedy’s audience continued to expand after a successful theatrical run, strengthening the case for its long-tail value to Disney.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Major League Soccer has named Los Angeles FC co-owner Larry Berg as its next commissioner, succeeding Don Garber on January 1, 2027. Berg will sell his stake in LAFC before taking the role, separating himself from ownership in one of the league’s clubs. The appointment sets up MLS’s leadership transition after Garber’s long tenure and puts an executive with direct experience in the league’s ownership ranks in charge of its next phase.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” opened to a record $360 million domestically and $932 million worldwide, Deadline reported. Its U.S. opening surpassed the $357.1 million debut of “Avengers: Endgame” in 2019, previously the domestic benchmark. The start gives the studios an unusually large theatrical launch and resets the standard for opening-weekend performance, though the film’s longer-term result will depend on whether it maintains audience demand beyond its first weekend.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet boosted recent quarterly profits with gains on stakes in private AI companies including OpenAI and Anthropic, whose valuations are now just below $1 trillion, CNBC reported. LSEG estimates S&P 500 earnings growth at roughly 48% year over year, but says growth is far weaker after removing gains from those investments. The accounting gains reflect rising portfolio values rather than revenue from software or services, complicating comparisons of Big Tech’s underlying operating performance.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants the Federal Reserve to expand a lending facility that could help Japan support the yen without disrupting the U.S. Treasury market, CNBC reported. Bessent said the United States intervened in currency markets to back the yen, an unusual step; the U.S. last joined a broader Japanese-support effort in 2011 after the earthquake and tsunami. Any Fed role could test its independence while affecting management of the roughly $29 trillion Treasury market.

stories.delivered_paragraph: CNBC’s Jim Cramer said Amazon CEO Andy Jassy’s latest earnings call shifted Wall Street’s view of Big Tech’s enormous AI spending by explaining how data-center investment could produce long-term cash flow. Amazon raised its capital-expenditure budget from $200 billion to $220 billion, yet its stock posted its biggest one-day gain in more than a decade. The market reaction suggests investors are becoming more willing to fund AI buildouts when companies provide clearer evidence of potential returns.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Treasury-market volatility is rising as investors position for higher yields in the roughly $30 trillion U.S. government-debt market, MarketWatch reported. Because Treasury yields set benchmark borrowing costs across mortgages, corporate debt and many other assets, sharp moves can quickly ripple through the wider financial system. The increased volatility leaves traders bracing for a more unsettled period in the market that anchors global borrowing and pricing.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Palantir shares rose after the company reported earnings, with its AI business driving what MarketWatch described as turbocharged growth. The market response highlights investor demand for companies showing commercial AI adoption, while placing added attention on whether Palantir can sustain that growth as more businesses build and manage their own AI systems.
